title: Choose the new look for Recalls Tutor
question: The roll assigned the Thumb-index handbook. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Thumb-index handbook
options.lineage: Pocket clinical handbooks with colour-cut thumb tabs
options.thesis: The QBank as a pocket handbook: every topic has its own coloured tab, so a student always knows where they are and what is left.
options.viewport: Outcome headline and exam picker on the left; an open handbook page on the right with a real sample question, its origin tags, and a column of gradient topic tabs cut into the page edge.
options.risk: Tabs become decoration if they stop navigating; on phones the tab column must become a bottom tab bar.

raised.raise: Every question carries its origin ticket: the sittings students recalled it from.
The accent gradient is spent only on the one action per screen; tab colours always mean topic, never emphasis.
Each tab shows what is still unanswered, so the gaps are always in view.
Topic performance reads as one row of identical tab meters, scanned at a glance.
Every state is shown by shape and label as well as colour, for bright light and colour-blind readers.

options.label: From the group chat to the bank
options.lineage: Study-group chat threads after an exam
options.thesis: Show the real mechanism: what a study group shares after the exam becomes organised, reviewed questions.
options.viewport: A chat thread on the left flows into clean question cards with sitting tags on the right, under one headline and a free-trial button.
options.risk: Familiar, and chat styling can read as a messaging app or suggest copied conversations.

options.label: Overlapping sittings
options.lineage: Translucent silk banners crossing a courtyard
options.thesis: Each sitting is a translucent colour band; where bands overlap, a question is high-yield.
options.viewport: Three soft sitting bands cross the screen behind the headline; a small legend explains that overlap means seen in both sittings.
options.case: Explains high-yield better than any other card, but students do not see themselves in it: it wins on product clarity, loses on audience identification.
options.risk: Abstract; it can look like decoration until the overlap is explained.

options.label: Moon-shadow bazaar
options.thesis: Questions as goods at a night market, each tagged with where it came from.
options.viewport: Stalls down one dark lane, each question ticketed.
options.case: Loses both axes: dreamlike, and nothing about it says exam preparation.
options.kept: Every question carries its origin ticket.

options.label: Centre-rail reference page
options.thesis: Dense twin columns around a rail of keys.
options.viewport: Two narrow columns with a red key rail between.
options.case: Loses both axes: scholarly and dense, the opposite of the simple, modern feel the CEO asked for.
options.kept: One accent, spent only on the action.

options.label: Video-store wall
options.thesis: Browse questions like spines on a shelf.
options.viewport: A wall of spines by topic.
options.case: Loses both axes: nostalgic entertainment, not professional study.
options.kept: What is missing shows as a visible gap.
options.risk: Playful to the point of unserious.

options.label: Meter bridge
options.thesis: Readiness as a row of needles leaning toward the pass mark.
options.viewport: A row of topic meters across the screen.
options.case: Loses both axes: a studio instrument, and readiness data does not exist yet for new visitors.
options.kept: Identical repeated meters, read in one sweep.

options.label: Exposure record sheets
options.thesis: Overlapping translucent sheets with hatching for state.
options.viewport: Stacked sheets over a tonal ramp.
options.case: Loses both axes: technical and grey, far from approachable.
options.kept: States shown by shape, not only colour.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A modern edtech SaaS page, executed cleanly: white, indigo-violet gradient, product screen in a soft card.
canonCard.viewport: Headline, sub-line and two buttons on the left; a sample question card on the right.
canonCard.risk: Looks like AMBOSS, Quesmed and every new QBank by design.
